_note: The EXECUTABLE READING of each executable entry's prose `applicability` block. It sits beside standard.json rather than inside it because `standard_hash` covers standard.json's canonical bytes, and a published citation resolves through that hash — adding predicates to the document would invalidate every citation already made against v1.0 to encode something the standard does not ASSERT. Where this file and the prose disagree, the prose is the standard and this file is the bug. `from` quotes the prose each rule reads, so the two can be checked against each other without opening both.

category._from: applicability_envelope.covers — 'Retail product pages selling roasted coffee to consumers as whole bean, ground, pods or capsules'
category._from_excludes: applicability_envelope.excludes — green coffee, instant/extract/chicory, RTD beverages, equipment and accessories, and coffee-FLAVOURED goods that are not coffee. Checked FIRST, because every one of these strings also contains the positive term: 'Coffee Grinder', 'Coffee Mug', 'Coffee Scented Candle'.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is roasted coffee sold by mass rather than in pods or capsules; does_not_apply_when: the product is a pod, capsule or pre-dosed sachet, where the state is inherent to the format
rules.satisfied_by_from: question: 'Can I buy this as whole beans?' Any of these names the same thing. Excluded deliberately: a bare 'Whole', which qualifies other nouns.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is roasted coffee sold by mass rather than in pods or capsules; does_not_apply_when: pods, capsules and pre-dosed sachets, where the coffee is ground by definition
rules.satisfied_by_from: question: 'Can I buy this already ground, so I do not need a grinder?' Every value here IS a grind, so a page offering one has answered yes even where no option is literally named 'Ground'. This is the FORMAT-002 half of the packet G-11 was built from: Bird Rock sells Whole Bean, Espresso and Filter, and was told it offers no ground coffee. Excluded deliberately: bare 'Medium', 'Fine' and 'Coarse', which are sizes on other stores.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is roasted coffee sold by mass and the seller offers any grind choice; does_not_apply_when: pods and capsules, where dose and grind are fixed by the format
rules.satisfied_by_from: question: 'Can I get this ground for espresso?' Deliberately NARROW: a generic 'Ground' option does not answer it, because the default grind of an unnamed ground option is the merchant's choice and is usually not espresso.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is roasted coffee sold by mass and the seller offers any grind choice; does_not_apply_when: pods and capsules
rules.satisfied_by_from: question: 'Can I get this ground for a filter or pour-over brewer?' Same narrowness as GRIND-001: a generic 'Ground' is left out because its grind is unstated.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is coffee sold by mass, INCLUDING pod packs that also declare a net weight — so this one deliberately does NOT take not_preportioned
applies_when: the product is roasted coffee offered to consumers in any format
rules.expectation_from: merchant_remediation: 'If a certifying agent certified the operation that packs this coffee, name that agent in product-page text alongside the legal operation name' — the condition is the standard's own. consumer_note adds that the word organic can be lawful without certification, so a page that does not use it is not necessarily withholding anything. Measured: 92 of 100 coffee stores state no organic claim (measured_discrimination, verdict not_discriminating), which is what 'most coffee is not certified organic' looks like from outside.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is roasted coffee offered to consumers in any format
rules.expectation_from: assertion is 'a fair-trade SCHEME claim is stated'. A roaster who buys outside any scheme has nothing to state, and 96 of 100 measured stores state nothing (verdict not_discriminating). Direct-trade and relationship-coffee buying are ordinary in this category and are not the scheme this entry names.

rules.from: applies_when: the product is roasted coffee offered to consumers in any format
rules.expectation_from: The entry's own question is 'Is this coffee from one place, or is it a blend?' — a question with two legitimate answers, only one of which this entry can evidence. merchant_remediation reads 'State the granularity and the named entity AT THAT LEVEL', which presupposes the lot is single-origin at all. A deliberate blend has answered the shopper correctly by being a blend.

rules.from: applies_when: the product page publishes readable Product structured data; does_not_apply_when: the page markup could not be read, which the engine reports as requiring store access rather than as an absence
applies_when: the product is physically shipped to the buyer; signal: any purchasable physical coffee product

_note_g11: G-11 additions. `expectation` is the executable reading of each entry's `merchant_remediation` prose, which the authors already wrote conditionally wherever the property may simply not hold ('IF a certifying agent certified the operation...') and unconditionally where every product in the envelope has it ('State the net quantity...'). It is read only for entries whose binding is req_kind 'claim', because that is the only kind whose absence can be the absence of a voluntary property; stating it on the others would be inert. `satisfied_by_option_values` names the option values that answer the same buyer QUESTION under a different word, which is category knowledge the engine has no way to derive and must not guess. Values are unambiguous on their own: a bare 'Medium' is a grind on one store and a size on the next, and a false equivalence here silences a true finding, which is the more expensive of the two errors.
